author: cushag
text: Once upon a day, there lived two people who were very poor. The husband used to go out and earn money while the wife had to look after their children. She was really fed up with her life as she could not get rid of all the household chores. One day, when they went to sleep, the woman thought that she should write something which would tell about her plight but then suddenly, she forgot what it was!

And when I have won and shall be known,

The world will know that it is all your own!

Why do we not hear from thee, O friend !

author: emily_dickinson
text:
The stars are beautiful with their shining light,
And it is pleasant on the mountain side.
On the top of the mountains they shine so bright;
I do not know why we love the sky above us.
Some things must be as they are;
We shall see what tomorrow will be.
But there are things that we can change now.

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
The night has gone, and still my eyes
Look far across the shining sea.
I see a ship at anchor there;

Its sails are furled with fading light:
It cannot flee from storm or tide,
But it is safe to shelter there!

Tigers are not meant to be tamed, yet people tame them
for their own pleasure and amusement. However, this is
not as simple or harmless as it may seem. The tiger does
not want to be with man, but he needs food to survive and
so must take what is offered him. For a tiger, being caught
is like death – so they are always on guard against
something that might capture them. A wild animal can never
be truly happy when forced into captivity by humans who
don't understand its ways or care about its well-being.

text: The words from which this little poem is written come from Shakespeare's Henry IV Part II (Act 2 Scene 4). They are spoken by one of the king's friends who tells Falstaff he knows all about the sea, and has been around it quite a lot - much more than Falstaff himself. The response is to write a short little poem using some of these lines as inspiration. It doesn't need to rhyme or anything too complicated - just have fun with them.

text:
O, Life! how sweet thy cup is when we sit at ease,

With all our cares and fears forgot !

Yet how oft thou giv’st us bitter drink to taste,

And sorrow like a cup doth fill our soul with woe !

author: thomas_hardy
text:
And it was so, for the son of God had gone up to Heaven;

and the hosts of the earth were divided into two parties ;
The one went down beneath the ocean, and became whales,
And seals, and fishes : they did not know that He was their Father.

But those who worshipped Him in the air became eagles
And ravens and nightingales ; while others who loved Him
Were turned into beasts or reptiles : all except some few
Who passed through the portals of His temples uncorrupted.

author: william_wordsworth
text:
The rosebud, which had blushed unseen,
 The heart that was but half given,

 The life that might have been complete, 
 The love that ne'er shall be mine! 

 In memory still I see her bloom, 

 And think, "How sweet it seemed!" 

 My hope is now a mournful dream — 

 It vanished and has never come.

Hiligaynon language is spoken by about 5 million people worldwide and is native to Panay Island, particularly Iloilo City.
